full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 226 of 2001 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Brahmanbaria for cancellation of Ewajnama Deed in respect of the suit property along with declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession. 

 6. Mr SM Abul Hossain learned Advocate appearing with Mr Md Golam Samdani learned Advocate submits that the Court of Appeal below being the final Court of fact neither discussed nor even mentioned the name of the PWs and DWs adduced by the parties nor mentioned the exhibits submitted by the parties neither gave independent findings in respect of the documentary and oral evidences and passed the Judgment and Decree in very slip-shod manner causing grave injustice to the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner which cannot be sustained in law. He further submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below miserably failed to consider that this suit being a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession through Court the suit has been filed within time and the Court of Appeal below being the final court of fact ought to have considered the case of either parties in juxtaposition of law. In the instant case, the Court of Appeal below neither discussed the evidences of parties at all nor mentioned the exhibits submitted by the respective parties. Non-consideration of the evidences on record and non-consideration of the exhibits filed by the respective parties independently the judgment and decree passed by the Court of Appeal below cannot be sustained in law. The learned Advocate then submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that the alleged Exchange Deed, Exhibit 4, fraudulently brought into existence covering only 52/ loo decimals of land with construction whereas the area of the suit land is. 65/100 decimals of land with construction, the excess land being not covered by the Exchange Deed Exhibit 4 should have been discussed and a finding in this regard ought to have been given by the learned Courts below the omission of which has rendered the impugned judgment and decree of the Courts below as illegal. He further submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that there cannot be any legally acceptable ground for the exchange of the suit land covered by the Exchange Deed Exhibit-4 situating at the heart of Brahmanbaria town, the value of which according to the purchase deeds of 1983 and 11987 (Exhibits 1 & 2 of 1983 and Exhibit 3 of 1987) standing in the name of the plaintiff's late husband is Taka (40,000 + 30,000 + 12,000) = 82,000 with the village land of Mouza Behair within Brahmanbaria Police Station the value of which is Taka 25,000 as stated in Exhibit 4. Besides this, the Behair Mouza village land of 5 decimals belonging to the defendant has been taken back by the defendant under an unregistered Deed Exhibit 5 in which there is only one witness but according to the section 3 of Transfer of Property Act at least 2 witnesses are necessary for any Deed and, as such, there should have been a finding that there has been no exchange at all of the suit land or any portion thereof under the alleged Exchange Deed Exhibit 4 with the Behair Mouza nal land of 5 decimals. He further submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that the Courts below ought to have come to the conclusion to the effect that the non-suited 5 decimals of nal land of Behair Mouza never came under the ownership and possession of the plaintiff's husband or the plaintiff and in such view of the matter, should have decreed the suit. He then submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that it is the settled principle of law that when both parties in a suit set up their independent claim to any property the onus becomes divided, that is to say, the plaintiff is to prove his plaint case and the defendant is to prove his defence case. He also submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that in the present suit onus being divided the plaintiff has discharged her burden by proving that the alleged Exchange Deed Exhibit 4 has been illegally brought into existences and the plaintiff's husband did not execute this alleged Exchange Deed Exhibit 4 and the plaintiff's husband did not go into possession and ownership of the Behair Mouza nal land of 5 decimals. Besides this, this 5 decimals of land also stands transferred to the defendant Exhibit Chha allegedly executed on 20-3-1992 and hence there has been no exchange of the properties between the parties and the aforesaid Exchange Deed has not been also acted upon and the defendant did not at all try to prove the execution of the suit Exchange Deed Exhibit 4 by the plaintiff's husband and so there has been failure on the part of the defendant to discharge his onus to prove the genuineness of the execution of the Exchange Deed. The learned Advocate submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that if really there would have been actually any Exchange of the properties between the plaintiff's husband and the defendant, the title deeds Exhibits 1, 2 and 3 of the suit land legally ought to have been in the custody of the defendant and on this count also the Courts below ought to have came to the conclusion that there has been no exchange of properties between the parties. He then submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that the entry of the defendant in the suit property as the ejectable monthly Bharatia under the plaintiff and the non-consideration of this aspect and the plaintiff has become the owner of the suit property by way of oral gift from her husband according to the provision of Muslim law and non- consideration of the aforesaid aspect in a lawful way has rendered the impugned judgments and decrees of the Court below illegal. Mr Hussain lastly submits that the Trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that the payment of Poura Taxes, creation of separation of Khatian, payment of rent of the suit land, papers relating to new survey, payment of electricity bill, etc all the papers marked as Exhibits for the defendant during illegal occupation of the suit land by the defendant and during pendency of the suit cannot at all be considered to be anything to confer any title to the suit property and, as such, committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
